sections.content: You know *deber*, *deberías* and *tener que* from B1 Unit 4. In bioethics and clinical writing, the choice between them marks the source of an obligation. *Deber* + infinitive expresses a moral, professional or deontological principle: what a code of ethics requires of a practitioner. *Tener que* + infinitive stresses an external, procedural or legal requirement imposed by an institution or regulation. For retrospective ethical judgement — evaluating what an institution failed to do — formal writing uses *debería haber* + past participle (rather than *tendría que haber* when stating a moral standard). In very formal codes, *haber de* + infinitive appears as a solemn synonym of *deber*.

sections.title: Four registers of obligation in bioethics
rows: Moral or professional duty (*El médico debe salvaguardar la confidencialidad.*)
External, legal or procedural requirement (*El hospital tiene que remitir el protocolo al comité de ética.*)
Retrospective ethical critique (*El centro debería haber revisado el código ético antes.*)
Solemn formal code (*Todo comité de ética ha de garantizar la imparcialidad.*)

items.spanish: La deontología establece que el médico debe proteger la confidencialidad del paciente.
items.english: Professional ethics establishes that the doctor must protect the patient's confidentiality.

items.spanish: Para aprobar el estudio, el hospital tiene que presentar toda la documentación ante el comité de ética.
items.english: To approve the study, the hospital has to submit all documentation to the ethics committee.

items.spanish: La clínica debería haber respetado la objeción de conciencia sin retrasar la atención.
items.english: The clinic should have respected conscientious objection without delaying care.

items.spanish: En bioética, toda norma ha de equilibrar los derechos individuales con el bien común.
items.english: In bioethics, every rule must balance individual rights with the common good.

sections.content: English speakers often use *deber de* + infinitive for strong obligation. In careful normative usage, *deber* without *de* expresses obligation (*debe cumplir el código ético*), whereas *deber de* expresses probability or conjecture (*debe de estar en consulta* = 'must be in consultation').
